name: HireVue
pros: Structured, documented scoring reduces unstructured interview variance
Scales initial screening across high-volume hiring
Bias audit tooling is more mature than most HR AI tools
files: Video interview recordings and game assessment responses.
value: Automated video interview analysis and game-based assessments for high-volume hiring. Reduces recruiter time on initial screening and provides structured, documented scoring. The governance burden is proportional to the volume of hiring decisions it touches.
engine: Computer vision, NLP, and IO psychology-grounded assessment models for interview analysis.
latency: Analysis completes after the interview, not in real time.
quality: Structured consistency is the proposition. The fairness and adverse impact questions are ongoing in both research and regulation, and are not resolved by any vendor.
tagline: Video interview and assessment AI, and the focus of more AI employment regulation than any other HR tool.
use_cases: High-volume first-round screening without live recruiter time
Structured scoring across a large candidate pool with documented rationale
Reducing unstructured interview variance in hiring decisions
integrations: Major ATS platforms (Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Taleo)
Background screening and offer management systems
governance_note: The most regulated AI tool in the HR category, by a significant margin. NYC Local Law 144 requires a bias audit before deployment in New York City and candidate notification. Illinois requires disclosure of AI use in video interviews. The EU AI Act classifies AI used in employment decisions as high-risk under Annex III. Several US states are moving on similar rules. The compliance checklist before deployment is jurisdictional-law-first, not vendor-capabilities-first: know which rules apply to your hiring locations, complete required audits, and establish candidate disclosure before turning it on. See the employment law pages in the reference library.
training_optout: Candidate data terms require explicit legal review. This is regulated data in multiple jurisdictions.
